item.title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
item.description: In a pivotal decision, the Delhi High Court has ruled in favor of the Socio Legal Information Centre, restoring its FCRA licence that was previously annulled by the Home Ministry. The court indicated that there was a lack of evidence to support accusations of the NGO's anti-government actions. Moreover, the court deemed the assertions of the NGO negatively impacting India's image on the global stage as without merit.
item.dc:creator: Abhinav Garg

item.title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
item.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that a judicial member must be present in the bench deciding asset attachments. This decision focuses on ensuring legal objectivity in the proceedings related to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments. The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions.

item.title: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
item.description: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has annulled the Bihar government's controversial decision to release Anand Mohan, who was serving time for murder. The state's attempt to modify prison regulations for his early exit was found unconstitutional. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
item.description: The Supreme Court has demanded that HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Home Finance provide unconditional sanctions. These sanctions involve officials implicated in collusion with builders in housing fraud schemes. The banks' CMDs must articulate their non-compliance in court if not met within a week. CBI’s investigations have led to chargesheets, and trials will commence once the necessary sanctions are secured, underscoring the urgency for timely judicial processes.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay Mahapatra

item.title: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
item.description: Mediation efforts between Rani Kapur and Priya Sachdev Kapur over Sunjay Kapur's estate ended without resolution. Former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, who mediated the dispute, reported reaching an impasse. Despite 15 sessions aimed at settlement, both parties did not show flexibility or understanding. The Supreme Court noted that no settlement can be forced upon unwilling parties. The court decided to close the mediation process and will issue a ruling soon.

item.title: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat
item.description: The call for a Parliament session by the BJP to discuss the delimitation bill has taken the opposition by surprise. As uncertainty looms, there are rising concerns among opposition parties about the potential impact on their voting power. The DMK, having previously opposed similar measures, now adopts a cautious stance. In contrast, Congress leaders maintain confidence, even as the government's influence grows.

item.title: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
item.description: Beginning November 30, the government is set to convene a brief session of Parliament focused on critical delimitation bills. These proposed laws are designed to establish a women's quota in the Lok Sabha by 2029, boosting its membership to 850 seats. Despite previous challenges in passing the bill, the government is optimistic about rallying support.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Rakesh

item.title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
item.description: The Supreme Court addressed concerns regarding the quality of food products offered by multinational companies in India. It emphasized the need for uniform standards across different countries to protect Indian consumers. The court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to enforce strict labeling regulations. Companies must not alter product compositions or conceal ingredient information. This ruling aims to ensure consumer health and transparency in labeling practices.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
item.description: The government plans to announce a pension scheme and health insurance for gig workers soon. Workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal will be the primary beneficiaries of these initiatives. The National Social Security Board will discuss contributory models, including a 2% turnover-based contribution from platforms. Trade unions have suggested immediate health and accident cover for these workers during onboarding.
item.dc:creator: Shiva Rajora

item.title: No content from Pakistan to be shown in India, government reminds Netflix
item.description: In a move reflecting ongoing tensions, the Indian Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has urged Netflix to limit access to Pakistani content, particularly an upcoming series set to debut on December 4. This action follows previous advisories related to national security concerns amid the India-Pakistan conflict. Netflix has not clarified the series' availability in India, as industry groups pursue legal actions against Pakistani media.

item.title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
item.description: The Supreme Court has instructed the FSSAI to implement front-of-package labeling within four months. Companies will have one year to comply with these regulations after the notification. Labels will indicate high levels of sugar, saturated fat, and salt inside red hexagonal shapes to protect consumer health. The court emphasized the importance of preventing public health crises associated with unhealthy food consumption.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Ex-terrorist fugitive’s 19-year run ends in arrest
item.description: Mohammad Mansha, a former terrorist, was arrested by a joint police team in Tral. He had evaded law enforcement for nearly two decades since laying down arms in 2007. Authorities revealed he was wanted in at least 13 criminal cases, including murder and conspiracy. His criminal activities included the killing of a police officer back in 2000. The operation involved meticulous planning and credible intelligence from various police units.
item.dc:creator: Sanjay Khajuria

item.title: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
item.description: The ongoing debate about heavy machinery's presence near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route is drawing intense scrutiny. Karan Singh pointed out that not all pilgrimage paths necessitate vehicle accessibility for pilgrims. Meanwhile, Mehbooba Mufti demanded transparency and public disclosure of any agreements linked to construction efforts. The J&K government refuted claims about construction, insisting that machinery is operating at a considerable distance.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
item.description: Germany's commitment to technology transfer under the P-75I submarine project with India is being emphasized. This partnership aims to enhance India's capabilities in undersea warfare technology, including Air-Independent Propulsion. Both nations share mutual trust regarding the protection of sensitive technologies and strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region. The deal may also lead India to become a hub for submarine manufacturing for Southeast Asian nations.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Parashar

item.title: Kashmir clerics split over Vande Mataram
item.description: A religious dispute over the national song Vande Mataram has intensified among clerics in Kashmir. Sunni scholar Maulana Abdul Rashid Dawoodi urged for a fatwa regarding standing during its rendition. Meanwhile, grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declared participation as impermissible under Islamic law. Several clerics expressed regret after attending a function where Vande Mataram was played. The controversy stems from a recent Union home ministry directive mandating its performance at official events.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: 30 missing ultras working from Pakistan & PoK to revive terrorism in J&K: Police
item.description: Thirty terrorists from Reasi district crossed over to Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir between 1991 and 2003. They obtained training and arms to launch activities against India while disrupting peace in Jammu and Kashmir. These individuals are now associated with Hizbul Mujahideen, facilitating the supply of arms and funds. Police have registered an FIR against them under various laws, including the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

item.title: I’m no troublemaker, won’t sign peace bond: Wangchuk
item.description: Sonam Wangchuk, representing the Leh Apex Body, was called upon by the district administration to discuss a peace bond. While he attended the meeting, Wangchuk declined to endorse any bond, deeming it unnecessary. He was given one week to address an extensive notice filled with allegations; however, his attorney later received a demand for a quicker response by November 28, prompting concerns about administrative transparency.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai

item.title: Road ministry tightens bidding norms to keep poor performers out of fully govt-funded projects
item.description: The road transport ministry has updated the bidding process for contractors to ensure better project execution. Performance ratings will now determine contractors’ eligibility for new projects, replacing the old financial year assessment approach. Stricter norms for joint ventures and improved technical eligibility conditions for major infrastructure projects have also been implemented. The revised Request for Proposal framework emphasizes transparency by requiring bidders to disclose ongoing disputes.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: Govt asks industry to curb urea diversion, cut costs as subsidy burden mounts
item.description: The government has called on the industry to cease the diversion of subsidised farm-grade urea for industrial purposes. Fertiliser secretary Rajat Kumar Mishra highlighted the disparity in pricing between agricultural and industrial-grade urea, urging adherence to misuse regulations. He expressed concern over fertiliser tagging practices by dealers that contribute to such diversion. The Fertiliser Association of India emphasized the need for increased domestic production and raw material diversification.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: India at disadvantage? US tariff uncertainty puts Indian exporters, buyers on edge
item.description: Indian exporters may face significant hurdles in the US market as new tariffs loom over their imports. Experts note that countries like Pakistan and Sri Lanka are not included in this investigation, likely giving them a competitive edge. A proposed 25 percent tariff could potentially decrease with future trade negotiations, leaving Indian businesses in a state of uncertainty regarding their trade dynamics with the US.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma
